title: Identity, Access Control, and Auditing
objective: Explain who can do what to which resources, as well as the roles of least privilege, policy evaluation, encryption, and auditing.

sections.title: How Much Access Should Be Granted, and to Whom?
paragraphs: In access control, first clarify who needs access, which resources they need to access, which operations they need to perform, and under what conditions. IAM principals include users and roles, and policies define permissions. The permissions an administrator needs are not the same as those required by a business application that uploads images.

The principle of least privilege means granting only the permissions necessary to achieve a purpose. For example, if an accounting employee only needs to view billing information, do not give them permission to delete resources as well. When a person’s or application’s role changes, review its permissions too.

When an application accesses AWS services, the basic approach is to use an IAM role with a limited purpose instead of embedding long-term credentials in the source code. Operational decisions include not only who uses the credentials, but also where they are managed and when permissions that are no longer needed should be removed.

sources.label: The principle of least privilege in AWS IAM

sections.title: Access Requests Are Evaluated Based on Context and Policies
paragraphs: When a principal requests an operation through the AWS Management Console, the CLI, or an API, AWS authenticates the principal as necessary and evaluates the request context and applicable policies to determine whether to allow or deny access to the target resource. When you see an access denial, do not simply conclude that permissions are missing. Instead, examine separately the requesting principal, the operation, the target resource, the applicable identity-based and resource-based policies, permissions boundaries, and organizational policies.

Identity-based policies and resource-based policies both affect permissions. If an applicable policy contains an explicit deny, that deny overrides any allow. Therefore, adding a broad allow in one place cannot cancel an explicit deny elsewhere.

In this unit, the goal is not to design complex policies, but to be able to articulate the information needed to make an access decision. Before changing permissions, users confirm the business need and scope of impact, and record the changes.

sections.title: Consider Protection and Accountability Separately
paragraphs: Protecting data involves more than encrypting it at rest and in transit; you must also decide who can read and write the data. For example, when storing inquiry records, verify the records’ confidentiality and intended use, then combine encryption with access controls that grant permissions only to the personnel who need them.

It is important not to confuse these roles. Amazon CloudWatch is used for monitoring with metrics, logs, and alarms; AWS CloudTrail is used to audit who performed which API operation and when; and AWS Config is used to understand resource configurations and their change history. Operations leaders should ensure that the necessary records can be reviewed during normal operations and determine retention periods and viewing permissions based on organizational requirements.

Compliance is not automatically achieved by choosing a particular service name. Users must review the applicable regulations, contracts, and internal policies. AWS Artifact is one place to review AWS compliance information, while AWS Config, CloudTrail, and CloudWatch handle evidence of configurations, operations, and operational status, respectively. Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, Amazon Inspector, AWS WAF, and AWS Shield are services that support protection and detection and should be combined according to the requirements.

sections.title: Combine protection, detection, and evidence according to their purposes
paragraphs: Security measures cannot be completed with a single service. AWS WAF controls requests to web applications, while AWS Shield helps protect against DDoS attacks. Amazon GuardDuty detects potential threats, Amazon Inspector helps manage workload vulnerabilities, and AWS Security Hub is compared as a service for aggregating security information.

Organizations combine services after clarifying what they need to protect, the threats involved, who is responsible after detection, and where evidence will be stored. Compliance information available through AWS Artifact is separate from evidence configured and operated by the organization itself. Organizations also review their requirements and potential impact before deciding how to respond to AWS Trusted Advisor recommendations.

The root user is not used for day-to-day operations and is protected with multifactor authentication. When handling multiple accounts or external identities, organizations compare IAM Identity Center, federation, cross-account roles, and similar approaches based on who needs access to what.

checkpoints.prompt: The photo-sharing service’s development team wants to grant only the image-conversion application permission to read the input prefix in a specific S3 bucket. Which action should the security team take based on the principle of least privilege?

choices.text: Grant the application administrator permissions that allow it to manage all AWS services.
choices.explanation: Administrator permissions that exceed what is necessary violate the principle of least privilege.

choices.text: Grant an IAM role restricted to the specific purpose only the permissions needed to read the input prefix in the target bucket.
choices.explanation: An S3 prefix is the leading portion of an object key. Granting the role a permissions policy limited to the principal, target resource, and operation follows the principle of least privilege. This role differs from a trust policy, which defines the principal that can assume the role.

choices.text: Store all developers’ personal credentials in the application’s configuration file.
choices.explanation: Sharing or embedding personal credentials undermines separation of use and credential management.

choices.text: Make the bucket public and allow the application to read from it without authentication.
choices.explanation: Public access does not meet the requirement to allow only the specific application to access the bucket.

checkpoints.prompt: An operations administrator received a report that an IAM role cannot read a specific S3 object. Before changing permissions, which information should be organized first?

choices.text: Confirm the requesting principal, the action performed, the target resource, and the applicable policies.
choices.explanation: Access decisions are based on the request context and applicable identity-based and resource-based policies, organization policies, permissions boundaries, and other factors. An explicit deny overrides an allow.

choices.text: Add the same permissions to all IAM users.
choices.explanation: Adding broad permissions without confirming the scope of the problem can violate least privilege.

choices.text: Delete and recreate every object in the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Deleting objects does not help identify the cause of the access evaluation and risks data loss.

choices.text: Ignore an explicit deny because it is always weaker than an allow.
choices.explanation: An applicable explicit deny overrides an allow and must not be ignored.

checkpoints.prompt: An employee responsible for auditing an online reservation service at a medical institution wants to be able to determine who changed critical settings in AWS and when. The data is already encrypted. Choose one additional measure.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail to review activity records, and manage record retention and viewing permissions according to the organization’s requirements.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail is used to audit who performed which API operations and when. Its purpose differs from CloudWatch monitoring and Config configuration history, and encryption alone cannot ensure accountability.

choices.text: Once encryption is enabled, records of who performed operations are no longer necessary.
choices.explanation: Encryption is one aspect of data protection and is separate from the function of recording the identities of operators and the times of their actions.

choices.text: Allow all users to freely change the settings subject to audit.
choices.explanation: Allowing unlimited parties to make changes undermines both least privilege and accountability.

choices.text: Create the necessary records only after a failure occurs.
choices.explanation: Because past activity records cannot be created after the fact, the system must be configured to record activity during normal operations.
